back: Animals, plants, fungi, prokaryotes (Prokaryotae or Monera) and protoctists (Protoctista or Protista).
Multicellular; cells with a nucleus but no cell wall or chlorophyll; feed on organic substances made by other organisms.
Multicellular; cells with a nucleus, cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts with chlorophyll; photosynthesise.
Usually made of hyphae (yeast is single-celled); cells with nuclei and chitin walls; no chlorophyll; saprotrophic or parasitic; store glycogen.
Single cells with no nucleus; circular DNA and plasmids; cell wall (not cellulose); no mitochondria.
Mostly single cells with a nucleus; some photosynthesise (*Chlorella*), some feed like animals (*Amoeba*, *Plasmodium*).

front: (Supplement) What is a virus made of?
back: Genetic material (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat.
notes: It reproduces only inside living host cells and is not placed in any kingdom.

back: Feeding on dead organic matter by releasing enzymes onto it and absorbing the soluble products.
Roots, stems and leaves (fronds); no flowers or seeds; reproduce by spores made on the underside of fronds.
Monocots: one cotyledon, parallel veins, flower parts in threes. Dicots: two cotyledons, branching veins, flower parts in fours or fives.
notes: Maize is a monocot; beans are dicots.

back: Thread-like filaments that make up the body of most fungi; a network of them is a mycelium.
